crons.name: HL Strategy Lab — Weekly Deep Eval

quality.reason: Well-structured output with clean formatting, links, engagement metrics, and one genuinely notable signal (HYPE ATH with high engagement), but the second tweet is pure hype noise and both entries are redundant celebratory content rather than actionable analysis.

Well-structured with concrete quantified metrics (PnL $-317.96, 44% WR, signal strengths, tagged news) that give real monitoring value, but rendering bugs like empty/malformed ticker tags [[]] and escaped quotes, sub-threshold signal strengths without action guidance, and truncation limit its actionability.

Well-structured review with quantitative strategy scores, confidence margins (BTC's thin +4.9 margin flagged with ⚠️), and trend deltas providing actionable signal for strategy assignment despite the flat, all-cash portfolio position.

The Discord report itself is well-structured with genuinely useful signals (flagged BTC/TAO orderbook imbalances, OI, funding rates in a clean table), but leaked internal progress text ('Wiki files written...') at the start mars the output and the signals lack explicit actionable guidance.

Well-structured digest with genuinely actionable anomaly flags (meta broken 136d, whale-mon 0% uptime, 94.8% signal bridge waste, stuck paper-trader), but chronic issues repeat daily without resolution, thresholds look inconsistent (arxiv 45.0 ✅ vs news 65.6 ⚠️), and negligible deltas like +0.2 dilute marginal daily signal.

Well-structured scan with transparent methodology disclosure, graceful degradation to web search when the arXiv API failed, and verified paper IDs with actionable metadata (links, authors, dates, categories) providing real research signal.

issues: Status line claims verification date of 2026-08-19, which cannot be confirmed and postdates verifiable releases of the referenced tools — the freshness stamp itself is untrustworthy and may be fabricated

Relies on niche third-party CLIs from personal Homebrew taps (antoniorodr/memo/memo, steipete/tap/remindctl, steipete/tap/imsg) that are not widely known or verifiable; personal taps are frequently abandoned or renamed — install URLs may be dead
Mainstream, better-maintained alternatives exist for these tasks (e.g., rgerganov/reminders-cli for Reminders, osascript/JXA directly for Notes and Messages) and are not mentioned

Status block contains environment-specific machine state ('imsg installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/imsg', 'memo and remindctl NOT installed') which will go stale immediately on any other machine and conflicts with the skill's own install instructions
Hard-coded path /opt/homebrew/bin/imsg assumes Apple Silicon Homebrew prefix; wrong on Intel Macs (/usr/local)
Verification claims ('All references/ docs verified present') reference relative files (references/apple-notes.md, references/apple-reminders.md) that cannot be validated from the provided content
Body is truncated mid-sentence in the iMessage section ('Permission: Gr'), so remaining sections, reference docs, and any additional tool sections could not be reviewed
Excerpt contains no URLs, so link rot cannot be assessed; full body should be checked for dead links

Claim 'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' is misleading — Anthropic ships a native computer-use tool type (since Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Oct 2024); reword to 'this skill does not require the Anthropic-native schema'
'Claude was trained on both' is an unverifiable training claim; Claude's official computer-use training targets screenshot-plus-coordinate actions, not this tool's element-index schema

Referenced techniques are current as of the review date (macOS AX API, Set-of-Mark prompting, OpenAI-compatible local endpoints, pyautogui contrast) — no deprecated tools or patterns found in the excerpt
Content is truncated mid-way through the actions table (cut at 'right_cic'); remaining actions and any version/permission notes cannot be evaluated
No mention of required macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions or macOS version constraints — a completeness gap affecting practical relevance
The computer_use tool described appears custom/first-party; freshness cannot be verified against an upstream canonical source
Content truncated at 2000 chars — remainder of body (including any external URLs or code examples) could not be reviewed for dead links or deprecated patterns
Claim that all 5 references/ files are 'verified present' is self-reported and cannot be confirmed from this excerpt
Inline dated update note in Loop Engineering Patterns row (Jul 4, 2026) is older than the doc-level review (Aug 23, 2026); embedded per-section dates risk drifting out of sync
Fleet implementation status markers (✅ Live) and 'fleet domains current' assertion are unverifiable and depend on external fleet state that may change independently of this doc
No external links or deprecated tooling visible in the shown portion (cron, Obsidian, LLM-loop patterns are current), but this cannot be guaranteed for the truncated portion
All three referenced tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode) are actively maintained as of latest knowledge; no deprecated tools detected

Codex CLI described as 'open-source' — OpenAI has shifted Codex CLI development toward a closed/private core repo while still publishing the @openai/codex npm package, so the 'open-source' framing may be slightly inaccurate now
OpenCode naming is ambiguous due to trademark dispute with the separate opencodefoundation/opencode project; reference file should pin the exact repo (sst/opencode) to avoid drift

No external URLs present in the excerpt, so no dead links — but the existence and freshness of references/claude-code.md, references/codex.md, references/opencodencode.md-adjacent files and the hermes-agent skill cannot be verified from this excerpt
'When to Use' section is a generic umbrella pointer with no tool-version pinning or last-verified dates, making future staleness hard to detect

CLI agent ecosystems move quickly (flag names, print/exec modes, TUI features change frequently); no mechanism noted for validating commands like print mode or worktree features still work as documented

References 'planned' cua-driver feature (Hermes autodetection) with a manual symlink workaround to ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver — this class of temporary workaround goes stale quickly; verify whether autodetection has shipped and the path is still correct

The 'cua-driver' tool name and its 'cua-driver skills install' command cannot be verified against the public trycua/cua repo; if the wrapper was renamed, merged into the main cua CLI, or deprecated, the install instructions are outdated
The trycua/cua project has iterated rapidly (shift toward the Liam agent product); the linked repo may be archived or restructured — confirm the link still points to maintained code
Claims 'Claude was trained on both' coordinate- and index-based clicking; harmless but an unverifiable model-training claim that ages poorly as models change
No version number, date stamp, or pinned release for the driver, so drift between this doc and the underlying tool cannot be detected from the doc itself

Otherwise the core patterns (SOM capture, AX/UIA/AT-SPI element-index clicking, cross-model/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, background accessibility-API automation vs pyautogui) are current, not deprecated

Core workflow (git merge/rebase conflict resolution, merge-queue arbiter pattern, multi-agent parallel campaigns) is current and relevant; no deprecated git commands or dead URLs appear in the visible excerpt

Heavy coupling to environment-specific tooling that cannot be verified against any public/standard API: `hermes kanban show <task-id>`, `kanban_create(title=..., assignee=..., parents=[...])`, and third-profile assignment assume a proprietary kanban CLI; if that CLI is renamed, versioned, or retired, the skill breaks silently with no fallback path

`delegate_task` does not match the subagent-spawning tool name in current major agent runtimes (e.g., Claude Code uses `Task`); confirm the tool name against the target runtime or document it as runtime-specific
Kanban API signature (`parents`, `assignee` parameters) is unpinned with no version reference or schema check, a common source of silent staleness in internal-tool docs
Prerequisites section makes kanban summaries a first-class input, but the doc's own fallback (PR bodies/commit messages) is buried; if the kanban tool is unavailable the skill reads as unrunnable
Only the first 2000 characters were reviewed; the Procedure section and any links, command examples, or tool invocations later in the body are unverified
